title: Immortal, Invisible, God Only Wise
description: Immortal, Invisible, God Only Wise in Tonic Solfa to ST DENIO, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, four verses and a piano.
about: Walter Chalmers Smith, a minister of the Free Church of Scotland, published this hymn on 1 Timothy 1:17 in Hymns of Christ and the Christian Life (1867). ST DENIO is a Welsh folk melody printed in John Roberts's Caniadau y Cyssegr in 1839.
underlay: Im-mor-tal, in-vis-i-ble, God on-ly wise, In light in-ac-ces-si-ble hid from our eyes, Most bless-ed, most glo-rious, the An-cient of Days, Al-might-y, vic-to-rious, Thy great name we praise.

lines: In light inaccessible hid from our eyes,
Most blessed, most glorious, the Ancient of Days,
Almighty, victorious, Thy great name we praise.
Unresting, unhasting, and silent as light,
Nor wanting, nor wasting, Thou rulest in might;
Thy justice like mountains high soaring above
Thy clouds which are fountains of goodness and love.
To all life Thou givest, to both great and small;
In all life Thou livest, the true life of all;
We blossom and flourish as leaves on the tree,
And wither and perish; but nought changeth Thee.
Great Father of glory, pure Father of light,
Thine angels adore Thee, all veiling their sight;
All laud we would render: O help us to see
’Tis only the splendour of light hideth Thee.
